message.content: Lions mate during a brief but intense courtship period that typically lasts only a few days. Male lions form coalitions—groups of related males that defend a pride together—and they compete for dominance within the coalition. When a male or coalition approaches a pride, he will engage in a series of displays: roaring loudly, scent-marking with urine and feces, and physically circling the females. If the female accepts, she will lie down and allow the male to mount her. The actual copulation usually lasts less than a minute, after which the male may leave or stay nearby to guard the females against rival males. This short mating window is followed by a gestation period of about 110 days before the cubs are born.
